page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-128 is a memory-allocated virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 128 virtual CPUs mapped to 64 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 864.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 6.75 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage for persistent disk volumes.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with the instance achieving top-tier ratings in Passmark CPU and encryption tests, alongside strong results in stress-ng multi-core evaluations. Memory subsystem performance is highly efficient, demonstrating strong read and write bandwidth under both cached and uncached large-block workloads. However, single-core performance remains in the average tier, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core metrics. This performance profile translates to strong capabilities in multi-threaded tasks like software compilation and ray tracing, while single-threaded execution speeds are moderate.

The n2-highmem-128 is optimized for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large-scale database operations, Redis deployments, and high-throughput static web serving. While it processes LLM prompts efficiently for small and medium models, its text generation performance for large 70B models is weak due to the lack of hardware GPU acceleration. This makes it highly cost-efficient for memory-dense, CPU-bound workloads and database caching layers, but less suitable for heavy generative AI inference tasks.
